project: NES Link Sprite Implementation – Pixel-Accurate Character Art
description: Replace procedural placeholder sprites with pixel-accurate NES Zelda Link sprites. Defines all Link movement, combat, item-use, and projectile frames as indexed-color pixel data rendered to HTMLCanvasElement, matching the original NES sprite sheet reference.

goal.ultimate: Implement all Link character sprites from the NES Zelda sprite sheet: basic movement (4 dir × 2 frames), item use (4 dir), item pickup (2 poses), magical shield (4 dir × 2 frames), sword attacks for 3 sword types (4 dir × ~4 frames each), magical rod (4 dir), weapon/projectile sprites (arrows, boomerang, sword beams, bombs, candle flame, rod beam), and hurt-state palette cycling (4 color variants).
constraints: Sprites are 16×16 pixels (matching PLAYER_SPRITE_WIDTH/HEIGHT in constants.ts)
Must use NES-authentic color palette (green tunic, tan skin, brown hair, dark outline)
Must pass all existing quality checks (typecheck, lint, test)
New sprites must register under existing SpriteKey values where applicable
New sprite keys for additional animations (shield, rod, sword types) extend the string map
Must not break existing animation system or rendering pipeline
Pixel data defined as indexed-color arrays, not loaded from external image files

context.referenceImage: NES Legend of Zelda Link sprite sheet showing all character frames organized by action category
context.spriteSize: 16×16 pixels per character frame (some weapon sprites are 8×8 or 8×16)
context.existingAnimations: src/animation/AnimationData.ts – defines idle, walk, attack, knockback, death, pickup animations
context.existingSpriteKeys: link_down_1/2, link_up_1/2, link_left_1/2, link_right_1/2, link_attack_down/up/left/right, sword_down/up/left/right, sword_beam
context.existingGbcModule: src/assets/gbc/ – GBC 2bpp sprite loader (completed, for Oracle characters)
context.renderer: src/rendering/SpriteRenderer.ts – renders sprites from assets.sprites map, supports flipX/flipY

basicMovement.description: Link walking in 4 directions, 2 frames each. Standard green tunic, no weapon drawn.

useItemWeapon.description: Link using a secondary item/weapon (B-button) in 4 directions. Arms extended holding item.

pickUpItem.description: Link holding item overhead. Frame 1: one-hand hold (small items like keys, rupees). Frame 2: two-hand hold (major items like Triforce, Heart Container).

magicalShield.description: Link walking with the Magical Shield (larger shield covering more of body). 4 directions × 2 frames.

woodenSword.description: Link attacking with the Wooden Sword. Each direction has ~4 animation frames showing the swing: pre-swing, mid-swing, full extension, recovery. The sword sprite is rendered as a separate element offset from Link's body.

whiteSword.description: Same attack animation structure as Wooden Sword but with a white/silver blade.

magicalSword.description: Same attack animation structure as Wooden Sword but with the Magical Sword (white blade with colored beam).
magicalSword.swordColor: Brown handle with white blade, emits sword beam at full health

magicalRod.description: Link using the Magical Rod in 4 directions. Similar animation to sword but with a rod (thin blue staff). Rod tip emits a magic projectile.
magicalRod.rodColor: Blue staff with blue orb tip

otherWeaponsItems.description: Standalone weapon and projectile sprites shown at bottom of sprite sheet.

hurtColorPalettes.description: Link's damage invincibility uses rapid palette cycling through 4 color variants. The sprite sheet shows these as: Palette 1 (normal green tunic), Palette 2 (blue/dark), Palette 3 (red/brown), Palette 4 (gray/white). Cycle order: 1→2→3→4→1 repeating every 4 frames during invincibility.

palettes.normal: Green tunic (#228B22), tan skin (#F5DEB3), brown hair (#8B4513), dark outline (#1A1A1A)
palettes.hurt_blue: Blue tunic (#4169E1), pale skin (#B0C4DE), dark hair (#191970), dark outline (#1A1A1A)
palettes.hurt_red: Red tunic (#CD5C5C), tan skin (#F5DEB3), dark red hair (#8B0000), dark outline (#1A1A1A)
palettes.hurt_white: White tunic (#C0C0C0), light skin (#FFFFFF), gray hair (#808080), dark outline (#1A1A1A)

userStories.title: NES sprite palette and pixel renderer module
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an NES sprite palette system and a pixel data renderer so that I can define sprites as compact indexed-color arrays and render them to HTMLCanvasElement. This is the foundation for all subsequent sprite stories.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/nes/NesPalette.ts exports NES Zelda color palettes: LINK_PALETTE (normal), LINK_HURT_BLUE, LINK_HURT_RED, LINK_HURT_WHITE, SWORD_PALETTE, ROD_PALETTE
Each palette is a tuple of RGBA colors indexed 0-N where index 0 is transparent
LINK_PALETTE contains: transparent, outline dark (#1A1A1A), tunic green (#228B22), skin tan (#DEB887), hair brown (#8B4513), tunic dark (#006400), shield orange (#CD853F), hat light (#32CD32)
src/assets/nes/NesPixelRenderer.ts exports renderPixelSprite(pixelData: number[], width: number, height: number, palette: RGBA[]) → HTMLCanvasElement
renderPixelSprite creates a canvas of the given dimensions and sets each pixel according to palette[pixelData[i]]
Index 0 pixels are fully transparent (alpha = 0)
Unit tests in tests/assets/nes/NesPalette.test.ts verify palette definitions (correct number of colors, index 0 transparent)
Unit tests in tests/assets/nes/NesPixelRenderer.test.ts verify canvas dimensions and correct pixel color mapping
npm run typecheck passes
npm run test passes
userStories.notes: Model the module after src/assets/gbc/ pattern. Use createImageData + putImageData for pixel-level rendering (same approach as GbcPalette.ts renderTileToCanvas).

userStories.title: Link basic movement sprites (walk 4 directions × 2 frames)
userStories.description: As a player, I want to see a pixel-accurate Link character when walking, replacing the colored rectangle placeholders. Define the 8 walk frames as indexed-color pixel arrays matching the 'Basic movement' section of the NES sprite sheet reference.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/nes/LinkMovementSprites.ts exports LINK_WALK_SPRITES: Record<string, number[]> with keys: walk_down_1, walk_down_2, walk_up_1, walk_up_2, walk_left_1, walk_left_2, walk_right_1, walk_right_2
Each pixel array is 256 entries (16×16) of palette indices referencing LINK_PALETTE
Sprites depict a recognizable Link character: green tunic/hat, tan skin, brown hair, facing the correct direction
walk_right frames can be horizontally flipped versions of walk_left (store one direction, flip at render time) OR defined separately
Walk frame 1 vs frame 2 show leg animation (alternating step positions)
Down-facing sprites show Link's face with eyes; up-facing sprites show back of head/hat
Unit tests in tests/assets/nes/LinkMovementSprites.test.ts verify: all 8 keys present, each array is length 256, all indices within LINK_PALETTE range
npm run typecheck passes
npm run test passes
userStories.notes: Reference the 'Basic movement' row of the sprite sheet. Each 16×16 sprite has index 0 for transparent border pixels. The NES Zelda Link is approximately 12×15 pixels of actual character within the 16×16 bounding box.

userStories.title: Hurt palette cycling system
userStories.description: As a player, I want Link to flash through different colors when taking damage, matching the NES behavior. Implement the 4-palette cycling system shown in the 'Hurt Colors Example' section of the reference sheet.
acceptanceCriteria: src/assets/nes/HurtPaletteSystem.ts exports createHurtVariant(basePixelData: number[], basePalette: RGBA[], hurtPalette: RGBA[]) → HTMLCanvasElement
createHurtVariant re-renders the sprite pixel data with the hurt palette substituted

Exports generateHurtSprites(spriteKey: string, basePixelData: number[], width: number, height: number) → Map<string, HTMLCanvasElement> that creates 3 hurt variants (blue, red, white) for a given sprite
Hurt variant keys follow pattern: {spriteKey}_hurt_blue, {spriteKey}_hurt_red, {spriteKey}_hurt_white
The 4 palettes cycle as: normal(frame 0) → blue(frame 1) → red(frame 2) → white(frame 3) → repeat, matching the Hurt Colors Example numbered 1→2→3→4→1

Exports getHurtSpriteKey(baseSpriteKey: string, frameCounter: number) → string that returns the correct hurt variant key based on cycling through the 4 palettes every INVINCIBILITY_FLASH_INTERVAL frames
Unit tests verify: hurt variants created with correct dimensions, palette cycling returns correct keys per frame counter, 3 variants generated per base sprite
npm run typecheck passes
npm run test passes
userStories.notes: The NES cycles Link through 4 color palettes during invincibility frames. INVINCIBILITY_FLASH_INTERVAL is 4 frames (from constants.ts). This replaces the simple flash-on/flash-off approach with authentic 4-color cycling.

userStories.title: Asset system integration — replace placeholders with NES sprites

Hurt variants from NES-007 are generated for all 8 walk sprites and registered (link_down_1_hurt_blue, etc.)
src/assets/nes/index.ts barrel-exports all NES module public APIs
src/assets/index.ts re-exports from ./nes
Main entry (main.ts or AssetGenerator.ts) calls loadNesLinkSprites() and merges results into assets.sprites, overwriting placeholder entries
